title: Operations are stored per (documentId, scope, branch) triple, and scope and branch live in OperationContext rather than on the operation
content:
The reactor's unit of storage is not the document — it is the `(documentId, scope, branch)` triple. Each triple maintains its own operation sequence, which is what lets a private draft in `local` and published content in `global` advance independently on the same document.

The operation itself is deliberately narrow:

```ts
type Operation = {
  id: string;              // stable derived operation id
  index: number;           // sequential index WITHIN the scope
  skip: number;            // skip count for reshuffle/undo
  timestampUtcMs: string;
  hash: string;            // content hash for verification
  error?: string;          // message from a failed action
  resultingState?: string; // serialized state after applying
  action: Action;
};
```

Note what is absent: **scope and branch are not fields on the operation.** They are carried in `OperationContext` alongside it. So `index` only means anything relative to a scope, and an operation moved between contexts would be meaningless — which is why the reactor always passes operations as `OperationWithContext`.

Four scopes are recognised by convention: `global` (shared state), `local` (per-user state such as preferences), `document` (system operations — `CREATE_DOCUMENT`, `DELETE_DOCUMENT`, `UPGRADE_DOCUMENT`, relationships), and any custom scope an application defines.
